title: Pasta al Limone
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Pasta al Limone is a bright, creamy Amalfi Coast classic — pasta tossed in butter, Parmigiano, and plenty of fresh lemon zest and juice for a dish that tastes like sunshine on a plate.
longDesc: This dish relies on the region's famous Sfusato Amalfitano lemons, prized for their thick, fragrant peel and balanced sweetness — the technique of emulsifying butter, cheese, and pasta water into a creamy sauce (without any actual cream) mirrors the logic of cacio e pepe, just with citrus in the starring role.
ingredients: 80 g (1 cup) finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, plus more for serving
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Fresh basil or parsley, torn, for garnish
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Reserve at least 1 cup of pasta water before draining.
In a large skillet, melt the butter over low heat.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet along with a splash of pasta water, tossing to coat.
Off the heat, gradually add the Parmigiano, tossing continuously and adding pasta water as needed to build a smooth, glossy emulsion.
Stir in the lemon zest and juice, tossing to combine.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil or parsley and extra Parmigiano.
chefTips: Zest the lemons before juicing them — it's much easier that way.
Add the lemon juice off the heat and at the end — direct heat can make citrus taste sharp and less fragrant.
Toss vigorously when combining the cheese to build a smooth, creamy emulsion rather than clumps.
commonMistakes: Adding the lemon juice too early or over too much heat, dulling its bright flavor.
Adding cheese directly to very hot pasta without care, risking clumping — work off the heat, as with cacio e pepe.
Using bottled lemon juice instead of fresh, which lacks the same bright, fragrant quality.
servedWith: A crisp white wine such as Falanghina
storage: Best eaten immediately — the emulsified sauce does not reheat well.
reheating: Not recommended; make fresh for the best texture.
healthBenefits: Vitamin C from the fresh lemon.
A good source of calcium from the Parmigiano.
culturalNote: This dish is deeply tied to the Amalfi Coast, where lemon trees cascade down terraced hillsides and the fruit is celebrated in everything from limoncello to this simple, elegant pasta.
